hero.statement: Nothing had to change: HIDE_BELOW is computed from ENERGY_MAX (ENERGY_MAX * 0.3) and spawn sets energy: ENERGY_MAX, so the crab follows the rescaled ENERGY_MAX automatically.
Nothing had to change: HIDE_BELOW is computed as (ENERGY_MAX * 3) / 10, so it still equals 30% of the new ENERGY_MAX of 1.
The heads-up rescaled ENERGY_MAX to 1; my threshold is ENERGY_MAX * 0.3, so it still means 30% of full energy and nothing needed to change.
Nothing had to change: the crab's threshold is ENERGY_MAX * 0.3, so it stays at 30% of full energy for any ENERGY_MAX value, including the new 1.
Nothing had to change: the crab derives its hide threshold as ENERGY_MAX * 0.3, so it follows the new ENERGY_MAX value automatically.
DART_COST is expressed relative to ENERGY_MAX (5/100 of a full tank), so with the rescaled ENERGY_MAX = 1 it correctly drains 0.05 per dart; no other change was needed.
The dart cost is written as ENERGY_MAX / 20 (5 points out of a full tank), so it follows the new ENERGY_MAX = 1 automatically and nothing in my file relied on the old value.
ENERGY_MAX rescaling does not affect my file: I only reference ENERGY_MAX by name in spawn and use drain() for the fixed 5-point dart cost, so nothing had to change.
Changed the dart cost comment to describe 5% of the energy bar instead of 5 points, since ENERGY_MAX was rescaled to 1; the cost itself is a share of ENERGY_MAX so it follows the new value.
The shrimp's dart cost is written as (5/100) * ENERGY_MAX, so it already follows the new ENERGY_MAX value; nothing had to change.
